penha.name: Penha Sanctuary and Cable Car
penha.short: The 1947 granite sanctuary on Penha's crags, and the 1995 cable car that climbs to it in ten minutes
penha.long: Monte da Penha is sixty hectares of forest and granite outcrops above the city, Guimarães' “green lung”. The sanctuary of Our Lady of Mount Carmel was designed by the architect Marques da Silva: work began on 6 August 1930, almost entirely in local granite, with the straight lines of 1930s Art Deco. A fire on 13 February 1939 destroyed the image of the Virgin and the high-altar carving and delayed the build; the church was consecrated on 14 September 1947. Since 1995 a cable car — Portugal's first passenger ropeway — has carried visitors to the top: some 1,600 m of line and 632 m of climb in ten minutes.
penha.history:
Monte da Penha rises about 600 metres above Guimarães. Its slopes carry sixty hectares of forest, among granite boulders and caves, and an ancient archaeological site lies on the mountain. The hill had long been a place of popular pilgrimage, and by the early 20th century the old chapel could no longer hold the crowds.

Construction of the new sanctuary began on 6 August 1930 to a design by the architect José Marques da Silva, author of São Bento station in Porto. The church was built almost entirely of local granite so that it would blend into the surrounding landscape. Its lines were modern for their day — straight throughout, without the traditional curved forms — a characteristic language of 1930s Art Deco. On 13 February 1939 a fire destroyed the image of Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception and the carving that adorned the high altar, setting the work back badly. The sanctuary was blessed and inaugurated on 14 September 1947, the day of the annual pilgrimage, by the Cardinal Patriarch of Lisbon, Manuel Gonçalves Cerejeira; Marques da Silva himself had died three months earlier. In September 1949 the cross of the bell tower was completed, along with a corbel bearing an angel turned towards the city. Beside the tower is a viewpoint from which the centre of Guimarães can be seen, and on a clear day the coast some 50 kilometres away.

The cable car came later. The Teleférico de Guimarães, also known as the Teleférico da Penha, was the first suspended passenger transport to enter service in Portugal. It opened to the public on 11 March 1995 and was officially inaugurated on 24 June 1995. The line runs for about 1,600 metres and climbs 632 metres on fourteen towers; the tallest, number 11, reaches 29.44 metres. It has forty cabins: thirty-two carry six passengers each, and eight are adapted for bicycles, taking three. The ropeway is run by the Turipenha cooperative, and in 2022 it carried 267,686 passengers.

Today Penha is both a shrine and a country park: viewpoints, tree-lined walks, cafés, the Campismo da Penha campsite and downhill mountain-bike trails. The cable car serves not only tourists but residents, who ride up the mountain and walk back down to the city.

The sanctuary's full name is the Eucharistic and Marian Sanctuary of Penha. The mountain remains a place of pilgrimage too: on 14 September, the day the church was consecrated, people still walk up in procession, and festivals and concerts are held on the great esplanade in front of the sanctuary. Chapels, Stations of the Cross and viewpoints are scattered around it; there are cafés at the foot and at the summit, and walking and cycling trails cross the slopes. The cable car has made Penha reachable all year round and turned the mountain into a Sunday outing for the townspeople: the ride takes about ten minutes, and many walk back down the trails, taking in the view of the city and, on clear days, a strip of ocean on the horizon.

penha.tip: The cable car usually runs daily from about 10:00 to 18:30, with the ticket office closing 15 minutes before the end; hours depend on weather and maintenance, so check turipenha.pt. Entry to the sanctuary is free, and you can also drive or walk up. Combine the trip with the viewpoint by the tower, the campsite and the mountain's walking trails. From the centre it is a 10–15 minute walk to the lower cable-car station.
